text:
Max Sasson became a Ranger on Nov 21, traded by Vancouver for a 2029 draft pick, and played his first game for New York the next afternoon against Carolina, centering Glenn Gawdin and Matt Rempe on the fourth line. Yahoo Sports wrote about the whirlwind 18 hours; Canucks teammates called him someone they all loved and appreciated in the room.

The move came the same day the Rangers announced Oliver Bjorkstrand and Alberts Smits would miss two to three months, per Mollie Walker of the New York Post. New York needed bodies up front.

What they're getting: a fast, undrafted 26-year-old who scored six goals in 24 games for Vancouver on 3.3 expected. He shot 21% last season too, so maybe he's a better finisher than average, but that rate rarely lasts. The Canucks also scored 15 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, one of the biggest gaps in the league.

NHL Edge has his acceleration at the 98th percentile. What to watch: whether the on-ice luck turns in a new city, and whether the fourth-line role grows.
